t: The Administrator shall make available upon request satellite imagery and aerial photography of remote terrain that NASA owns at the time of the request to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, or the Director of the Five Star Medallion Program, to assist and train pilots in navigating challenging topographical features of such terrain.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that sharing imagery with the Director of the Five Star Medallion Program, who may be a non-federal actor, counts as coordination with an outside party. But the section only requires NASA to hand over existing imagery on request to help train pilots. No outside party is consulted or heard before a federal decision, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. The other recipient, the FAA Administrator, is inside the federal government.
fable.s: The Administrator shall make available upon request satellite imagery and aerial photography of remote terrain that NASA owns at the time of the request to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, or the Director of the Five Star Medallion Program

qwen_block.w: This section describes the sharing of data between federal agencies (NASA and the FAA) or with a specific program director. It does not involve consultation with or participation by entities outside the federal government, such as the general public, states, or private companies, in a decision-making process. The 'Five Star Medallion Program' is likely an internal or specific program, and even if it involves pilots, the text only mandates data availability for training, not a participatory decision-making role for outsiders.
qwen_block.s: The Administrator shall make available upon request satellite imagery and aerial photography of remote terrain that NASA owns at the time of the request to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, or the Director of the Five Star Medallion Program, to assist and train pilots in navigating challenging topographical features of such terrain.

opus.w: The section only requires NASA to share existing imagery, when asked, with the FAA (a federal agency) or the Five Star Medallion Program, to help train pilots. Even if the Medallion Program is outside the federal government, it is only receiving data. It is not consulted, does not advise, and has no means to challenge a federal decision. Mentioning an outside recipient is not enough to count as participation.
opus.s: The Administrator shall make available upon request satellite imagery and aerial photography of remote terrain that NASA owns at the time of the request to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration, or the Director of the Five Star Medallion Program
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions an outside party: the Five Star Medallion Program, a private Alaska aviation-safety program. That reading fails because this party does not take part in any federal decision. NASA simply has to hand over imagery it already owns when asked. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory role or right to object. A request for existing data is closer to a request for a service or benefit than to a say in a decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section authorizes the NASA Administrator to provide data to the FAA Administrator, who is a federal official inside the government. Coordination or data sharing between federal agencies does not constitute participation as defined. The other recipient, the Director of the Five Star Medallion Program, is not clearly an outside entity involved in a decision-making process, and the action is a unilateral provision of data rather than consultation or advisory input.

The "Director of the Five Star Medallion Program" is likely a federal program director or an internal designation, and even if it were an outside entity, the text describes a unilateral provision of data ("make available upon request") rather than a collaborative decision-making process, advisory role, or consultation before a federal decision.
